topLine: Former NSW opposition leader Mark Speakman has announced he will not recontest his seat in March, becoming the eighth of 24 Liberal lower house MPs to head for the exit, with leader Kellie Sloane saying she is "pretty sure" the departures are now over. The Guardian argues the Coalition's troubles are opening space not only for One Nation but for teal-style independents in Sydney. Locally, the South Coast Register reports Shoalhaven Council's improved finances have eased fears of large rate rises, while the council's mayor has publicly called on Liza Butler MP to explain an unspecified matter.

briefing.topLine: Former NSW opposition leader Mark Speakman has announced he will not recontest his seat in March, becoming the eighth of 24 Liberal lower house MPs to head for the exit, with leader Kellie Sloane saying she is "pretty sure" the departures are now over. The Guardian argues the Coalition's troubles are opening space not only for One Nation but for teal-style independents in Sydney. Locally, the South Coast Register reports Shoalhaven Council's improved finances have eased fears of large rate rises, while the council's mayor has publicly called on Liza Butler MP to explain an unspecified matter.
briefing.localWatch: Shoalhaven ratepayers get some reassurance, with the council reporting an improved financial position that reduces the prospect of steep rate increases, even as Mayor White publicly presses Liza Butler MP for an explanation. The Illawarra Mercury also reports a NSW Health plan to use Shellharbour Hospital as an aged care site to move older patients out of the region's hospitals sooner.

stories.headline: Huge rate rise fears eased as council turns around its financial position
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports that fears of large rate rises in Shoalhaven have eased after the council improved its financial position through what the paper describes as tough fiscal management.

stories.headline: Mayor White calls on Liza Butler MP to please explain
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council has published a statement in which Mayor White calls on Liza Butler MP to "please explain". No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: The Shellharbour solution to get stranded seniors out of hospital sooner
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports NSW Health plans to turn Shellharbour Hospital into an aged care site, as growing numbers of older people remain stranded in the region's hospitals.

stories.headline: Council wins second major award for innovative housing development
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council reports it has received a second major award for an innovative housing development. No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: Community invited to help shape future of Cudmirrah Hall
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council is inviting community input on the future of Cudmirrah Hall, according to a council notice.

stories.headline: Kellie Sloane says she’s ‘pretty sure’ NSW Liberals exodus is over after Mark Speakman resigns
stories.summary: Former opposition leader Mark Speakman told the final sitting day of the Legislative Assembly before the March election that he will not recontest his seat, making him the eighth of 24 Liberal lower house MPs not to run again. The Guardian reports he warned his party against becoming "One Nation lite", while current leader Kellie Sloane said she is "pretty sure" the departures have now stopped. The ABC reports Sloane said she did "everything" to try to stop Speakman quitting, with the party trailing Labor and One Nation in the polls.

stories.headline: Treasury says Minns’ Woollahra redevelopment plans are not achievable
stories.summary: The Australian Financial Review reports that confidential advice to the NSW government warned it would not be possible to build around 9,000 dwellings in the Woollahra area, given high land values and split ownership, after Labor said the area would get 9,400 new homes.

stories.headline: ‘Underpaying’ firm on Western Sydney International Airport metro line bought Rolls-Royce, Porsche
stories.summary: The AFR reports funding talks between the NSW government and contractor WeBuild over the Western Sydney Airport metro have collapsed, with the government citing concerns about subcontractor compliance amid a dispute over a cost blowout at an airport metro stop.

stories.headline: Minns government launches taskforce on modern slavery
stories.summary: The Australian reports the Minns government has set up a multi-agency taskforce to tackle modern slavery in NSW.

stories.headline: Explosive kidnap extortion allegation in berry heartland: report
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that an anti-slavery report has prompted police referrals over alleged kidnapping on the Coffs Coast in northern NSW. Only the headline was available; the allegations are untested.

stories.headline: Spitting, swearing, death threats: Life as a political staffer
stories.summary: The ABC reports that the union representing staff working for NSW politicians says their members are facing "unprecedented" levels of violence, with staffers raising security concerns.

stories.headline: Wollongong green energy company axes jobs months after $49 million grant
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that Wollongong green energy firm Hysata has cut jobs months after receiving a $49 million government grant, with its chief executive saying the workforce is "evolving, not contracting".

stories.headline: Body worn cameras rolling out for NSW hospital security staff
stories.summary: The NSW government has announced body worn cameras will be rolled out to all security staff in NSW hospitals, which it says will help de-escalate violent incidents.

stories.headline: Vape users hospitalised after losing consciousness, prompting public health warning in New South Wales
stories.summary: NSW Health has issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate after three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised tested positive for the substance, The Guardian reports. Officials say etomidate is a fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but is not registered for medical use in Australia.

stories.headline: Government feud leaves no Sydney Origin listed on draw
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports the NRL has warned State of Origin could be moved out of NSW if a deal cannot be reached, with no Sydney match listed on the draw amid a dispute involving the government.

stories.headline: More than 400 new homes set for St Leonards
stories.summary: The NSW government says developer Deicorp has been selected to build more than 400 homes on surplus government land at St Leonards identified through its property audit.

stories.headline: Exterior completed on $105 million Moree Hospital Redevelopment
stories.summary: Health Infrastructure says the façade of the new building at Moree Hospital in northern NSW is now complete as part of the $105 million redevelopment.

stories.headline: Sydney councils push for powers to limit number of e-bikes on city streets
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports Sydney councils want new powers to manage share e-bikes, with demands including a cap on fleet numbers, penalties for poorly parked bikes and an age limit.

stories.headline: Who pays the bills? Beached whale removal costs see council demand reform
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Wollongong City Council is seeking statewide support for a new approach to who pays for removing whale carcasses from beaches.

stories.headline: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: the teals
stories.summary: The Guardian argues that the NSW opposition's difficulties are creating an opening for progressive independents in Sydney, on top of the challenge from One Nation, and says those independents are being helped by Premier Chris Minns, whom it describes as a shrewd political operator.

stories.headline: The Snoop: Bosses cop a spray at Walkleys, government responds to AI-slop funding claims, and more
stories.summary: Crikey's gossip column covers the Walkley Awards, the government's response to claims about news innovation funding and AI-generated content, Greens calls for whistleblower protections in sport following the sandpaper controversy, and a return of the Democratic Labour Party.

elsewhere.text: Victoria: new modelling reported by The Australian suggests the state's debt could reach $259 billion by 2036, with the paper arguing growth alone will not resolve it — a reminder of how state balance sheets are shaping political debate.
